definition: In mathematics, mirror descent is an iterative optimization algorithm for finding a local minimum of a differentiable function.
details: It generalizes algorithms such as gradient descent and multiplicative weights.

explainer.lead: Mirror descent is an iterative optimization algorithm for finding a local minimum of a differentiable function. It matters as a generalization of familiar methods such as gradient descent and multiplicative weights.

tiers.eli5: It's a way of walking downhill to find a low point, taking steps shaped to fit the terrain rather than always straight along the slope.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it as a generalization of gradient descent when the geometry of the problem favors a different step rule. A pitfall is the added complexity of choosing the mirror setup compared with plain gradient descent.
tiers.paperLevel: It is an iterative optimization algorithm for finding a local minimum of a differentiable function; it generalizes gradient descent and multiplicative weights. No formula or convergence bounds are given.

explainer.example: An optimization problem solved with multiplicative weights is treated as a special case of the more general mirror descent procedure.
